doc.title: SparseRoute: Adaptive Sparsity for Efficient Neural Machine Translation

bullets: SparseRoute adds a learned top-2 router that activates only a subset of feed-forward blocks, reducing the compute needed per translated token.
On WMT14 English–German the method lowers median inference latency by 42% while keeping BLEU within 0.3 points of a dense Transformer baseline.
The evidence is limited to a single-GPU lab setting; energy savings and low-resource generalization are claimed but not directly measured.
summary.eli5: Imagine a translation model as a large team of specialists. SparseRoute gives every word a small switchboard that wakes only the two specialists it needs, instead of waking the whole team. On one benchmark it made translation about 42% faster while keeping quality almost the same.

claims.text: SparseRoute reduces inference latency by 42% compared with the dense Transformer baseline.

evidence.text: On WMT14 En–De, SparseRoute lowered median latency from 120 ms to 70 ms per sentence (42.1% reduction) while BLEU changed by 0.2 points.
Latency was measured with batch size 16 on a single A100; the router itself adds 4.1% overhead.

claims.text: The method maintains BLEU within 0.3 points of the dense model on WMT14 English–German.

evidence.text: BLEU on WMT14 En–De: 28.7 for the dense baseline and 28.4 for SparseRoute, a difference of 0.3 points.

claims.text: SparseRoute can cut energy consumption by up to 60% in data-centre deployments.

evidence.text: Energy per generated token fell by 57% on a single A100 in our lab; we did not measure routing overhead in a data-centre network.

report.markdown:
# Executive Report - SparseRoute: Adaptive Sparsity for Efficient Neural Machine Translation

**Source:** `sparseroute-demo.pdf` - 9 pages - about 22 min read
**Readiness:** TRL 4/9 - Technology validated in lab
**Reproducibility:** 63/100 - 5 present, 3 partial, 4 missing.
**Claim check:** 2 supported - 2 partial - 2 insufficient

## 1. What the paper achieved
- Reports 4,812 words across 7 detected sections; estimated reading time 22 min [p.1].
- Key concepts extracted from the text include WMT14, English–German, SparseRoute, Transformer, BLEU. [p.2]
- 2 of 6 extracted claims cleared the evidence threshold; 2 were partially supported and 2 remained unverified.
- Reproducibility audit scored 63/100 (5 present, 3 partial, 4 missing).
- Readiness assessment: TRL 4/9 - Technology validated in lab [p.6].

## 2. What is proven
- SparseRoute reduces inference latency by 42% compared with the dense Transformer baseline. [p.6]
- The method maintains BLEU within 0.3 points of the dense model on WMT14 English–German. [p.7]

## 3. What is not proven
- SparseRoute can cut energy consumption by up to 60% in data-centre deployments. [p.8] The evidence reports 57% on one GPU, not “up to 60%” in data-centre conditions. [p.8]
- The approach may generalize to low-resource language pairs. [p.8] The paper explicitly limits evaluation to two high-resource pairs. [p.8]

## 4. Main risks
- Random seed is not reported, so independent reproduction is harder.
- The software environment is only partially documented.
- Readiness stops at TRL 4; no field or operational evidence was found.

## 5. Recommended next steps
- Report full hyperparameters and random seeds so results can be repeated.
- Run a field/pilot evaluation to move beyond TRL 4.
- Clarify the scope of the energy claim with a direct data-centre experiment [p.8].

## Appendix - at a glance
- Datasets: WMT14, English–German, English–French
- Models & methods: SparseRoute, Transformer, top-2 gate
- Metrics: BLEU, latency, F1
- Technical-term density: 0.071
- Complexity score: 6.8/10
- Reproducibility note: Text-level audit only; no code was executed.
- TRL note: No field/pilot evidence was found.
